items.prompt: A signal has sensitivity 0.9 but the condition is rare. What else is needed to compute P(condition|positive)?

options.text: The prior and false-positive rate as well
options.why: They determine how positive mass splits across the partition.

options.text: Only sensitivity; reverse conditionals are always equal
options.why: That would ignore the base rate and false signals.

options.text: Only the prior, because every positive signal is equally informative
options.why: The false-positive rate determines the positive mass contributed by the complement; the prior alone cannot supply it.

options.text: Only specificity, without the prior or sensitivity
options.why: Specificity gives the complement of the false-positive rate, but both true-positive mass and the prior are still needed.

items.explanation: The posterior denominator includes positive mass from both the condition and its complement.
